description: Space Trainers es un grupo que busca desarrollar un entrenamiento para astronautas, adaptado para las exigencias físicas que hay fuera de la Tierra. Con esta investigación buscamos mejorar su rendimiento y adaptación en el espacio.
summary: This project developed a comprehensive physical conditioning program for astronauts, based on the principles of sports planning and integrating physiological, technical, and nutritional criteria. Structured in an 18-week macrocycle under the contemporary A.T.R. model —Accumulation, Transformation, and Realization— it strategically distributes volume and intensity to optimize performance. It includes a total load of 1000 kilometers of aerobic endurance and 1920 minutes of strength training, in addition to autonomous scuba diving in a pool as a microgravity simulation for physical and mental preparation. The proposal addresses the physiological alterations caused by microgravity during space missions, such as cardiovascular imbalances, headaches, sleep disorders, weight loss, muscle atrophy, bone demineralization, and orthostatic intolerance upon returning to Earth. It includes specific activities on land and in aquatic environments to develop aerobic endurance, strength, balance, coordination, and agility, reinforcing pre-mission preparation. In this way, it seeks to minimize the negative effects of microgravity, recognizing that the success of future space missions largely depends on the physical and functional health, effective, safe, and sustainable, of the crew.
details:
This project is designed to properly guide the physical conditioning of an astronaut prior to undertaking a space mission, through a systematically and properly structured program, planned as an 18-week macrocycle, following the modern A.T.R. training model (Accumulation, Transformation, and Realization).

The program is implemented through activities organized into three major blocks, referred to as mesocycles: Accumulation (5 weeks), Transformation (6 weeks), and Realization (7 weeks). The program primarily considers a total training load of 1000 kilometers for the development of aerobic endurance, and 1920 minutes for strength development. Additionally, it includes two autonomous diving sessions, scheduled in weeks 7 and 14, to simulate space-like conditions.

Each mesocycle is composed of microcycles—weekly units with six days of training—which may be categorized as adjustment, load, impact, or recovery weeks, depending on the dynamics of volume and intensity.

⦁ Aerobic endurance is trained on Monday, Wednesday, and Friday with 60-minute sessions.

⦁ Strength training takes place on Tuesday, Thursday, and Saturday, also in 60-minute sessions, incorporating UDT amphibious gymnastics, a method used by members of the Navy SEALs, elite special operations units from World War II, who are considered pioneers in modern underwater combat.

Each training session follows a consistent sequence:

⦁ 10 minutes of warm-up, including joint mobility and low-intensity aerobic exercises to activate the cardiorespiratory system.

⦁ 40-minute main session:

⦁ Aerobic training intensity is guided by the Borg Rating of Perceived Exertion (RPE).

⦁ Strength training progresses through strength endurance, maximum strength, and explosive strength phases.

⦁ 10 minutes of cool-down, focusing on muscle stretching exercises.

Practical and scientific relevance:

This project aims to offer a practical and understandable guide for the necessary physical activity involved in astronaut conditioning—one that is dynamic and motivating. The program is based on scientifically grounded training principles and also incorporates military-proven methods from UDT amphibious training and autonomous diving exercises, which closely simulate space conditions.

Ensuring astronaut health is crucial for the success of future space missions, and this program contributes directly to maintaining and enhancing crew readiness.

Planning Tools Used

The 18-week macrocycle was designed using Microsoft Excel, and the preparation of astronauts for the diving sessions was supported with a training chart based on the UDT amphibious gymnastics method, as used by U.S. Navy SEALs special operations forces.
